input: What does v-prediction predict, and why is it useful for video generation?
expected_output: v-prediction predicts v = alpha_t * epsilon - sigma_t * x, an interpolation between the noise and the data. It is useful for video generation because it has been shown to help avoid color shift compared to epsilon-parameterization.

input: What architecture does Sora use?
expected_output: Sora uses the DiT (Diffusion Transformer) architecture, which operates on spacetime patches of video and image latent codes. Visual input is represented as a sequence of spacetime patches that act as Transformer input tokens.

input: How many diffusion models does Imagen Video use in total?
expected_output: Imagen Video uses 7 diffusion models in total: a base video diffusion model plus a cascade of 3 temporal super-resolution (TSR) and 3 spatial super-resolution (SSR) models. It also uses a frozen T5 text encoder for conditioning.

input: In Imagen Video, how does SSR differ from TSR in the upsampling step?
expected_output: SSR (spatial super-resolution) upsamples by bilinear resizing, while TSR (temporal super-resolution) upsamples by repeating frames or filling in blank frames.

input: How does Text2Video-Zero generate video without any training?
expected_output: Text2Video-Zero uses two mechanisms. First, it samples the sequence of latent codes with motion dynamics to keep the global scene and background time-consistent. Second, it reprograms frame-level self-attention into a cross-frame attention where each frame attends to the first frame, preserving the context, appearance and identity of the foreground object.

input: What three mechanisms does ControlVideo add on top of ControlNet?
expected_output: ControlVideo adds three mechanisms: cross-frame attention that introduces interactions between all frames at all time steps, an interleaved-frame smoother that interpolates alternating frames to reduce flickering, and a hierarchical sampler that splits long videos into short clips with pre-generated key frames for long-term consistency.

input: What is Lumiere's STUNet architecture and what does it remove?
expected_output: Lumiere uses a space-time U-Net (STUNet) that generates the entire temporal duration of the video at once in a single pass. This removes the dependency on temporal super-resolution (TSR) components.

input: What are the three training stages for Stable Video Diffusion?
expected_output: The three stages are: text-to-image pretraining (improves quality and prompt following), video pretraining (at a larger scale on a curated dataset), and high-quality video finetuning on a smaller, pre-captioned, high-fidelity dataset.

input: What are the three components of Agentic Context Engineering (ACE)?
expected_output: ACE has three components: a Generator that produces task trajectories referencing bullet points, a Reflector that distills insights from successful and failed trajectories, and a Curator that updates the structured context with incremental, itemized entries.

input: What does Meta-Harness optimize?
expected_output: Meta-Harness optimizes the code that determines and optimizes what information should be stored, retrieved and presented to the model. It is described as a harness for optimizing harnesses; its proposer is itself a coding agent and its output is a collection of harness candidates on the Pareto frontier.

input: Why does the file-system-as-persistent-memory pattern exist?
expected_output: Because a harness should not carry the entire workflow and all logs in context. In long-horizon agentic rollouts, artifacts such as experiment logs, code diffs, error traces and past trajectories grow much longer than the context window, so durable state should be kept in files.

input: What is the goal of the Self-Taught Optimizer (STOP)?
expected_output: STOP's goal is not directly to improve the solution s, but to improve the improver I itself through recursive scaffolding, using meta-utility measured across a collection of downstream tasks.

input: What did the STOP experiments find about weaker base models?
expected_output: STOP improved mean downstream performance across iterations with GPT-4 but degraded with weaker models such as GPT-3.5 and Mixtral, implying that recursive structure alone is not enough and the base model must be capable enough to improve the mechanism.

input: What are the seven components of a harness in Agentic Harness Engineering (AHE)?
expected_output: The seven components are: system prompt, tool description, tool implementation, middleware, skill, sub-agent configuration, and long-term memory.

input: What is the Darwin Gödel Machine (DGM) and what did it achieve?
expected_output: DGM explicitly targets the evolution of an editable harness-code repository with an LLM coding agent that is allowed to modify its own harness. With Claude 3.5 Sonnet as the base model, the discovered agents were comparable to or outperformed handcrafted agents on SWE-bench Verified (20% to 50%) and Polyglot (14.2% to 30.7%).

input: Compare the architecture choices of Sora and Imagen Video.
expected_output: Imagen Video is built on a 3D U-Net architecture: a cascade of diffusion models including a base model plus 3 spatial and 3 temporal super-resolution models, using progressive distillation down to 8 sampling steps. Sora instead uses a Diffusion Transformer (DiT) that operates on spacetime patches of video and image latent codes as Transformer input tokens.

input: How do Text2Video-Zero and ControlVideo differ in their cross-frame attention?
expected_output: Text2Video-Zero configures all frames to attend only to the first frame. ControlVideo adds fully cross-frame interaction, introducing interactions between all frames at all time steps by mapping the latent frames into query, key and value matrices.

input: Compare ACE and Meta Context Engineering (MCE).
expected_output: ACE treats context as an evolving playbook and learns insights from rollouts, but its update rules and overall workflow are still handcrafted: a Curator emits structured itemized bullets merged with deterministic logic to avoid context collapse. MCE separates the mechanism of how to manage context from the artifact content, running skill evolution at a meta-optimization level and context optimization at a base level, using free-form skills rather than enforced heuristic structure.

input: How do Video LDM and Stable Video Diffusion differ in what they fine-tune?
expected_output: Video LDM keeps the pretrained image backbone frozen and only fine-tunes the newly added temporal layers, plus a temporally fine-tuned decoder. SVD uses the same architectural idea of inserting temporal layers but fine-tunes the entire model.

input: What is the author's view on whether RSI will come from the harness layer or the core model?
expected_output: The author's near-term prediction is that harness engineering will evolve toward meta-methodology, with the harness itself becoming an optimization target. Eventually many harness improvements may be internalized into core model behavior, but the interface with external context and tools should remain, similar to how prompt engineering became less central while the need to specify goals, constraints, context and evaluation did not disappear.
